6932-pictures-every-child-should-know-a-.title: Pictures Every Child Should Know A Selection Of The World S
6932-pictures-every-child-should-know-a-.creator: Unknown
6932-pictures-every-child-should-know-a-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Indian pottery was the first development of art in America and it led to the working of metals, followed by drawing and portraiture. Among the Americans, as soon as that term ceased to mean Indians, art took a most distracting turn.

arxiv-1809-06700.title: Π \Pi -cyc: A Reference-free SNP Discovery Application using Parallel Graph Search
arxiv-1809-06700.creator: Reda Younsi 1*, Jing Tang 2 and Liisa Holm 1
arxiv-1809-06700.description: Abstract Motivation: Working with a large number of genomes simultaneously is of great interest in genetic population and comparative genomics research. Bubbles discovery in multi-genomes coloured de bruijn graph for de novo genome assembly is a problem that can be translated to cycles enumeration in graph theory. Cycle enumerations algorithms in big and complex de Bruijn graphs are time consuming.

arxiv-2201-11134.title: Dust and the intrinsic spectral index of quasar variations: hints of finite stress at the innermost stable circular orbit 2022 Dust and the intrinsic spectral index of quasar variations: hints of finite stress at the innermost stable circular orbit – 13
arxiv-2201-11134.creator: John R. Weaver, Keith Horne
arxiv-2201-11134.description: Abstract We present a study of 9 242 spectroscopically-confirmed quasars with multi-epoch ugriz photometry from the SDSS Southern Survey. By fitting a separable linear model to each quasar’s spectral variations, we decompose their five-band spectral energy distributions into variable (disc) and non-variable (host galaxy) components.

arxiv-2212-12474.title: Physics-Informed Gaussian Process Regression Generalizes Linear PDE Solvers
arxiv-2212-12474.creator: Marvin Pförtner marvin.pfoertner@uni-tuebingen.de, Ingo Steinwart ingo.steinwart@mathematik.uni-stuttgart.de, Philipp Hennig philipp.hennig@uni-tuebingen.de, Jonathan Wenger jonathan.wenger@uni-tuebingen.de, [0.5em] University of Tübingen, Tübingen AI Center
arxiv-2212-12474.description: Abstract Linear partial differential equations (PDEs) are an important, widely applied class of mechanistic models, describing physical processes such as heat transfer, electromagnetism, and wave propagation. In practice, specialized numerical methods based on discretization are used to solve PDEs. They generally use an estimate of the unknown model parameters and, if available, physical measurements for initialization.

arxiv-2305-15702.title: Microcanonical Truncations of Observables in Quantum Chaotic Systems
arxiv-2305-15702.creator: Fernando Iniguez, Mark Srednicki
arxiv-2305-15702.description: Abstract We consider the properties of an observable (such as a single spin component that squares to the identity) when expressed as a matrix in the basis of energy eigenstates, and then truncated to a microcanonical slice of energies of varying width.

arxiv-2306-04497.title: Data structures for photoabsorption within the ExoMol project
arxiv-2306-04497.creator: Jonathan Tennyson, Marco Pezzella, Jingxin Zhang and Sergei N. Yurchenko Department of Physics and Astronomy, University College London, Gower Street, WC1E 6BT London, United Kingdom
arxiv-2306-04497.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jonathan Tennyson, Marco Pezzella, Jingxin Zhang and Sergei N. Yurchenko Department of Physics and Astronomy, University College London, Gower Street, WC1E 6BT London, United Kingdom. The ExoMol database currently provides comprehensive line lists for modelling the spectroscopic properties of molecules in hot atmospheres.

arxiv-2307-03422.title: Pulsar discovery prospect of FASTA
arxiv-2307-03422.creator: Mengyao Xue, Weiwei Zhu, Xiangping Wu, Renxin Xu, Hongguang Wang
arxiv-2307-03422.description: Abstract The Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) has discovered more than 650 new pulsars, which account for 20% of our known Galactic pulsar population. In this paper, we estimate the prospect of a pulsar survey with a radio telescope array to be planned — the FAST Array (FASTA), consists of six ”FAST-type” telescopes.

arxiv-2404-12002.title: Comparing the three-dimensional morphological asymmetries in the ejecta of Kepler and Tycho in X-rays
arxiv-2404-12002.creator: A. Picquenot 1,2,3, T. Holland-Ashford 4, B. J. Williams
arxiv-2404-12002.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by A. Picquenot 1,2,3, T. Holland-Ashford 4, B. J. Williams. Recent simulations have shown that asymmetries in the ejecta distribution of supernova remnants (SNRs) may be a reflection of asymmetries left over from the initial supernova explosion. Thus, SNR studies provide a vital means for testing and constraining model predictions in relation to the distribution of heavy elements, which are key to improving our understanding of the explosion mechanisms in Type Ia supernovae.

arxiv-2501-01363.title: On orthogonal factorization systems and double categories
arxiv-2501-01363.creator: Branko Juran
arxiv-2501-01363.description: Abstract We prove that the ∞ \infty -category of orthogonal factorization systems embeds fully faithfully into the ∞ \infty -category of double ∞ \infty -categories. Moreover, we prove an (un)straightening equivalence for double ∞ \infty -categories, which restricts to an (un)straightening equivalence for op-Gray fibrations and curved orthofibrations of orthogonal factorization systems.

arxiv-2508-15091.title: Visualizing Poloidal Orientation in DNA Minicircles
arxiv-2508-15091.creator: Tony Lemos, Harold D. Kim
arxiv-2508-15091.description: Abstract A short ( < < 150 bp) double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) molecule ligated end-to-end forms a DNA minicircle. Due to sequence-dependent, nonuniform bending energetics, such a minicircle is predicted to adopt a certain inside-out orientation, known as the poloidal orientation. Despite theoretical and computational predictions, experimental evidence for this phenomenon has been lacking.

arxiv-2509-21534.title: A circuit for predicting hierarchical structure in-context in Large Language Models
arxiv-2509-21534.creator: Tankred Saanum, Can Demircan, Samuel J. Gershman & Eric Schulz, Harvard University, Institute for Human-Centered AI, Helmholtz Computational Health Center
arxiv-2509-21534.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at in-context learning, the ability to use information provided as context to improve prediction of future tokens. Induction heads have been argued to play a crucial role for in-context learning in Transformer Language Models. These attention heads make a token attend to successors of past occurrences of the same token in the input.

arxiv-2602-08052.title: Graph-Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Objective Unrelated Parallel Machine Scheduling
arxiv-2602-08052.creator: Bulent Soykan, Sean Mondesire, Ghaith Rabadi, Grace Bochenek
arxiv-2602-08052.description: Abstract The Unrelated Parallel Machine Scheduling Problem (UPMSP) with release dates, setups, and eligibility constraints presents a significant multi-objective challenge. Traditional methods struggle to balance minimizing Total Weighted Tardiness (TWT) and Total Setup Time (TST). This paper proposes a Deep Reinforcement Learning framework using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and a Graph Neural Network (GNN).

pmc-11327895.title: Socioeconomic inequalities in the relationship between internet usage patterns and depressive symptoms: Evidence from a Chinese longitudinal study
pmc-11327895.creator: Ting Wang, Shouchuang Zhang, Qiaosheng Li, Haoran Liu, Shan Zhang, Weiyan Jian, Jing Guo
pmc-11327895.description: BackgroundThe increasing prevalence of depressive symptoms has emerged as a critical public health issue globally, highlighting the need for analyses of the factors contributing to depressive symptoms within the Chinese population and the development of targeted recommendations for improving mental well-being.

pmc-11466611.title: Comparative genomics of two protozoans Dictyostelium discoideum and Plasmodium falciparum reveals conserved as well as distinct regulatory pathways crucial for exploring novel therapeutic targets for Malaria
pmc-11466611.creator: Shivam Nanda, Rajan Pandey, Rahila Sardar, Ashutosh Panda, Aruna Naorem, Dinesh Gupta, Pawan Malhotra
pmc-11466611.description: Plasmodium falciparum, which causes life-threatening cerebral malaria has rapidly gained resistance against most frontline anti-malarial drugs, thereby generating an urgent need to develop novel therapeutic approaches. Conducting in-depth investigations on Plasmodium in its native form is challenging, thereby necessitating the requirement of an efficient model system.

pmc-11514420.title: Systemic treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma secondary to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
pmc-11514420.creator: Karolina Rzeniewicz, Rohini Sharma
pmc-11514420.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third leading cause of cancer death globally, with 15% of cases arising on a background of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). NAFLD is a heterogenous condition ranging from fatty liver to cirrhosis and is itself a growing global problem, with estimated worldwide prevalence of 50% in 2040.

pmc-11650788.title: Associations Between Labor Control Through Digital Platforms and Workers' Mental Wellbeing: A Survey of Location-based Platform Workers in Taiwan
pmc-11650788.creator: Yawen Cheng, Wan-Ju Cheng, Ro-Ting Lin, Yi-Ting Wang, Jyh-Jer Roger Ko
pmc-11650788.description: BackgroundPlatform work offers flexibility and autonomy to workers, but there are concerns about the impacts of excessive labor control exercised by digital platforms using algorithmic management. This study assessed the level of labor control exerted by digital platforms and explored its associations with psychosocial work conditions and workers' mental well-being.

pmc-12507517.title: Teamwork of clustered low-affinity κB sites and accessory factors regulates transcriptional strength of NF-κB RelA dimers
pmc-12507517.creator: Shandy Shahabi, Tapan Biswas, Yuting Shen, Rose Sanahmadi, Yaya Zou, Gourisankar Ghosh
pmc-12507517.description: Non-consensus binding sites of transcription factors (TFs) are often observed within the regulatory elements of genes; however, their effect on transcriptional strength is unclear. Within the promoters and enhancers of NF-κB-responsive genes, we identified clusters of non-consensus κB DNA sites, many exhibiting low affinity for NF-κB in vitro. Deletion of these sites demonstrated their collective critical role in transcription.

pmc-12800326.title: Modelling dysfunction-specific interventions for seizure termination in epilepsy
pmc-12800326.creator: Aravind Kumar Kamaraj, Matthew Parker Szuromi
pmc-12800326.description: Epileptic seizures result from abnormal synchronous neuronal firing caused by an imbalance between excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission. While most seizures are self-limiting, those lasting over five minutes, termed status epilepticus, require medical intervention. Benzodiazepines, the first-line treatment, terminate seizures by enhancing GABAergic inhibition, but fail in approximately 36% of cases.

pmc-12859913.title: Exploring the future of the diagnostic process in primary care
pmc-12859913.creator: Esmée W P Vaes, Esther de Groot, Siamack Sabrkhany, Ton Bruining, Jochen W L Cals, Dorien Zwart, Alma C van de Pol
pmc-12859913.description: BackgroundOver the past years many innovations are being developed aiming to improve diagnostic processes in primary care. Limited evidence is available on how those actually involved in those processes, in short-hand end-users (patients, general practitioners, and medical specialists such as radiologists), view innovation of the diagnostic process in primary care.

pmc-12966581.title: Heterozygous X-linked Alport syndrome in a pregnant woman: A case report
pmc-12966581.creator: Caroline Gee, Matthew D Nguyen, Dao Le, Ramy Hanna
pmc-12966581.description: Alport syndrome is a genetic disorder of chronic kidney disease, hearing loss, and ocular abnormalities, caused by mutations in type IV collagen. While X-linked Alport Syndrome demonstrates characteristic severe renal failure in males, it has a variable presentation in females.

pmc-12967537.title: Impact of sulfamethoxazole, trimethoprim, diclofenac, carbamazepine, and their mixture on the metabolism of Lemna minor: a targeted metabonomic study
pmc-12967537.creator: Rofida Wahman, Peter Schröder, Geoffroy Duporté, Serge Chiron, Jörg Drewes, Andrés Sauvêtre, Catarina Cruzeiro
pmc-12967537.description: IntroductionMetabolomics is an analytical profiling technique that measures and compares large numbers of metabolites in biological samples, providing insight into metabolic mechanisms. There are few studies concerning the effects of xenobiotics and their transformation products on aquatic plant metabolites, which can uptake and detoxify them using untargeted metabolomics.

pmc-13289418.title: The value of preoperative CD4+ T-cell count in predicting infectious complications after endoscopic lithotripsy for upper urinary tract calculi among human immunodeficiency virus-infected patients
pmc-13289418.creator: Penghui Lai, Enming Shao, Zhe Zhu, Jun Ma, Kewen Chen, Wei Wang
pmc-13289418.description: BackgroundTo explore whether preoperative CD4+ T-cell count is associated with postoperative infectious outcomes after endoscopic lithotripsy for upper urinary tract calculi in human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-infected patients.MethodsThe HIV-infected patients who underwent endoscopic lithotripsy for upper urinary tract stones at Shanghai Public Health Clinical Center from May 2019 to May 2025 were enrolled for this study.

pmc-13315971.creator: Ivan Camilo Sanchez-Rojas, Catherin Lorena Solarte-Jimenez, Nery Astrid Pabón-Cadena, Andres Rodriguez-Cardona, Derlis Caicedo-Triana, Lina Cristina Bravo-Muñoz, Darío S. pmc-13350569.title: Podcast: Immune Persistence After Primary Vaccination with MenQuadfi
pmc-13350569.creator: Mika Rämet, Mike Simon
pmc-13350569.description: Invasive meningococcal disease (IMD) remains a serious global health concern. Although incidence is generally low, the disease progresses rapidly and carries high fatality rates of 10–15%, with survivors often experiencing long-term sequelae including hearing loss, neurological impairment, or limb amputations. These consequences highlight the need for effective and durable vaccination strategies. IMD incidence and serogroup distribution vary geographically.

pmc-13515869.title: XYL-1 and Olaparib Synergistically Inhibit the Growth of Pancreatic Cancer by Suppressing the SCD1/BRCA1 Signaling Pathway
pmc-13515869.creator: Ye Yang, Lei Huang, Yaru Du, Qingyue Zhu, Li Dai, Bingjun Qian
pmc-13515869.description: PARP1/2 inhibitors have received FDA approval for pancreatic cancer harboring BRCA1/2 mutations and homologous recombination (HR) deficiency; however, their limited indications restrict their broader clinical application. Previous studies have demonstrated that PARP7, a member of the PARP family, enhances tumor sensitivity to PARP1/2 inhibition. However, the mechanisms underlying their synergistic effects in pancreatic cancer remain unclear.
